question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 1,000 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before May 2026?
summary: Early-2026 pace (~606 deaths by end-February) implies a non-trivial chance of reaching 1,000 by end-April if March and April stay high.
Objections highlight realistic downside risks: potential March–April underperformance, provisional data revisions, and SAR/policy changes that could dampen fatalities.
Historical baselines (roughly 2,100–2,450 annual deaths) make the threshold plausible but not guaranteed, given month-to-month volatility.
The ensemble signal remains strong, but a modest downward calibration accounts for the identified downside risks without assuming implausible scenarios.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and reveal real downside risks (pace sustainability, data revisions, SAR/policy dynamics) but do not negate the core signal; a modest downward adjustment is warranted.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted from 0.92 to 0.84 to incorporate downside risks from pace sustainability, provisional data revisions, and potential policy/SAR changes; the range encapsulates remaining uncertainty. No physically implausible scenario was assumed.

causal-factors.name: Early-2026 pace through February (≈606 deaths/missing by Feb 24)
causal-factors.rationale: If the February pace persists into March–April, total Mediterranean deaths by May will likely exceed 1,000.

causal-factors.name: Historical annual base rate for Mediterranean fatalities
causal-factors.rationale: Historical totals around 2,100–2,450 per year imply that reaching 1,000 by May is plausible given a continued high early-year pace.

causal-factors.name: Central Mediterranean route risk / seasonal pattern
causal-factors.rationale: The Central Mediterranean remains the deadliest route with ongoing fatalities in late winter–spring, raising the odds of hitting 1,000 by May.

causal-factors.name: Potential improvements in search-and-rescue or policy interventions
causal-factors.rationale: Enhanced SAR capacity or safer legal channels could reduce fatalities, lowering the likelihood of reaching 1,000 by May.

causal-factors.rationale: Early-year counts can be revised as more data arrive, introducing uncertainty about the exact total by May.

causal-factors.name: Adverse weather / sea conditions
causal-factors.rationale: Storms or rough seas could increase fatalities, pushing totals above 1,000 if conditions worsen.

causal-factors.name: Pace of Mediterranean fatalities in early 2026
causal-factors.rationale: 606 deaths/missing by end-February 2026 (AP News) and over 600 by February (The Guardian) imply that if March–April maintain a similar pace, crossing 1,000 by May is plausible.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate and year-to-date headroom
causal-factors.rationale: Historical IOM tallies hover around 2,100–2,450 Mediterranean deaths annually (including about 2,108 in 2025 per L'Orient-Le Jour), so reaching 1,000 by May would be feasible within the annual scale.

causal-factors.name: Data gaps and reporting delays that could suppress May tallies
causal-factors.rationale: Missing Migrants counts can undercount or lag in reporting; the 2025 data were described as potentially higher, indicating uncertainty that could keep May tallies below 1,000 if delays persist.

causal-factors.name: Pace of Mediterranean fatalities in early 2026
causal-factors.rationale: As of late February 2026, at least 606 migrants have died or gone missing in the Mediterranean, the deadliest start to a year since IOM began recording in 2014, implying momentum toward 1,000+ by May if the pace persists.

causal-factors.name: Seasonal/worsening weather and spring migration patterns
causal-factors.rationale: Spring is typically a period of higher activity and risk on the Central Mediterranean, which could sustain or raise the death toll in 2026.

causal-factors.name: Undercounting and reporting gaps (missing at sea)
causal-factors.rationale: IOM and media reports note hundreds more missing at sea that cannot yet be verified, suggesting totals could rise beyond confirmed deaths.

causal-factors.name: Policy/SAR dynamics (crackdowns vs rescue capacity)
causal-factors.rationale: Stronger EU/Italy migration controls and any constraints on search-and-rescue could reduce crossing attempts or survival rates, dampening the near-term fatalities.

synthesis: The ensemble strongly suggests a high likelihood of surpassing 1,000 deaths by May if the March–April window maintains a high pace, but real downside risks from data revisions and policy/SAR dynamics justify a modest discount. Calibrated probability reflects these uncertainties while maintaining a high overall confidence in the signal.
